Nice job on failing on the OHP! Seriously, you're not really getting stronger unless you push to failure occasionally.

Also notable, when you're lifting your body will hold more water (glycogen) for energy. It's definitely not uncommon to hold onto a few extra lbs and then all of a sudden be 5lbs lighter. Look up the "whoosh effect". If you're staying within your boundaries you're doing okay!

The 5k, something you might try is c25k. I know you can already run the 5k but this program will allow you to run at a full pace for shorter bursts and build on top of that. If you're trying to get a better time this may help out to start from ground zero instead of just trying to get a little bit faster every day. Or when you're running take 30 second bursts and run at full stride and then let yourself recover. That's where you want to be in the end, running it in full stride all the way through.
